lines: Ah, a customer with a pulse. How refreshing.
Duskhollow is where the dead gather. Not mindlessly — they remember.
The corruption here doesn't destroy. It preserves. Every soul trapped between was and wasn't.
A kingdom of almost-people, Shopkeeper. And they all have stories they can't finish.
Make yourself at home. Such as it is.
No formal address. The handwriting is unsteady.
You know, don't you. What I did. What I am.
I wanted to save my line. My father's legacy. Instead I broke the world and condemned its people to this... half-existence.
The man in the void — the Strategist — he was my friend once. My closest advisor. I drove him to this.
If you can stop him without the Grail, perhaps that is enough.
Perhaps rebuilding is enough.
— No signature
dialogs.notes: First genuine vulnerability from the King. Personal, handwritten, no royal pretense.

lines: The air shimmers at the edge of camp. A translucent figure appears — a woman in scholar's robes, her expression caught between warning and sorrow.
She looks at you. Through you. As if searching for someone who isn't there.
Her lips move, but no sound comes. Only a faint hum — like crystal vibrating at the edge of hearing.
Then she turns toward the deeper halls. Points. And fades.
Your heroes exchange uneasy glances. The air smells of old parchment and ozone.
dialogs.notes: Lira's ghost. She appears as a vision on floor 2 of the Necropolis dungeon. Does not speak — communicates through gesture. Points deeper, toward where the Sovereign's camp scene happens on floor 4. Players who pay attention will connect her to Valdric's story two floors later.

lines: Her name was Lira.
She was the finest mind in the kingdom. She warned the King the Grail was unstable.
He ordered the activation anyway.
She was standing next to it.
I remember her. Across every rewrite, every shattered timeline. I remember her because the void burned her into me.
The King gets to forget. I do not.
That is why the Grail must be mine. Not revenge. Correction.
dialogs.notes: Full portrait, standing before you. His voice breaks, just slightly, on 'standing next to it.' Then cold again. The most human the villain gets.

lines: Six regions. Six puppets. You are remarkably persistent for a merchant.
One region remains. The void's heart. My domain.
Come if you dare, Shopkeeper.
But know this — everything you've built, every town, every hero, every supply line — exists because I allow it.
That courtesy ends now.
dialogs.notes: Full presence. Grudging respect turns to direct threat.

lines: Cedric arrives in civilian clothes. No tabard. No royal seal.
I've resigned my commission.
The King's cause is just — his guilt is real. But I cannot serve a crown that hides the truth from the people fighting for it.
I'm not leaving, Shopkeeper. I'll fight alongside you.
Not for the Crown. For the towns. For what you've built.
dialogs.notes: Major character moment for Cedric. He becomes an ally, not a mouthpiece.
